subject: INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE function
notes:
⛔ OVERTURNED: PARTIAL -> DIVERGES. The adjudicator listed the week-date CRASH as its OWN reason (1) for the verdict and then rounded down. A returned value that is not produced AT ALL, for legal in-range §15.3.1.7-permissible input, is a DIVERGENCE. PARTIAL is for a half that was not checked; this half was checked and is wrong.

CITATIONS RE-VALIDATED BY ME: cite.py --check 15.48.4 "The returned value is the integer date form equivalent of the date represented by argument-2 when analyzed according to argument-1." -> OK (§15.48.4 1)). cite.py --check 15.48.1 "The type of this function is integer." -> OK - UNCONDITIONALLY integer, unlike §15.39.1's argument-dependent result-type table, so the national-result mislabel that holds FORMATTED-DATE's RV row at PARTIAL cannot arise here; the adjudicator was right to leave it out and I confirmed why. cite.py --check 15.3 "If the evaluation of an argument results in an incorrect value" -> OK (§15.3 rule 14).

THE DIVERGENCE, derived from the code and the calendar - not sampled, because the program COMPILES and only faults at run time. For "YYYYWwwD" with argument-2 "9999W526" or "9999W527", every §15.3.1.7 subfield rule is satisfied (year 9999 is > 1600 and <= 9999; 9999 is a 52-week ISO year so week 52 is inside 01..52; day-of-week 6 and 7 are inside 1..7), so §15.48.3 r4 is MET and §15.48.4 r1 governs and demands a returned value. Analyze's `else if (hasWeek) integerDate = (ISOWeek.ToDateTime(yy, wk, wd == 7 ? DayOfWeek.Sunday : (DayOfWeek)wd) - Epoch).Days + 1;` computes ordinal = 52*7 + d - (jan4DayOfWeek(9999) + 3) = 360 + d against a 365-day year, i.e. 10000-01-01 and 10000-01-02, and throws System.ArgumentOutOfRangeException. NO VALUE IS RETURNED AND NO COBOL EXCEPTION CONDITION IS RAISED. §15.3 rule 14 forecloses the last escape - read in full it covers an incorrect value "for that argument OR FOR THE RETURNED VALUE" and prescribes EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION or, with checking disabled, the implementor-defined result - so even on the most conservative reading (that the denoted date has no integer date form, §15.5.2 topping out at 3,067,671) a raw CLR stack trace is not a permitted disposition. Same single root cause as AR-15.48.3-4/-5 - ONE fix, bound-check the week-date reconstruction; do not count it three times. The verdict is recorded HERE because it is this rule's RETURNED VALUE that goes missing.

WHAT IS CORRECT, re-verified by READING the conversion rather than by trying values (the PB5 lesson): Analyze reconstructs the date from whichever subfields the format carries - calendar `new DateTime(yy,mo,dm)`, ordinal `new DateTime(yy,1,1).AddDays(doy-1)`, week `ISOWeek.ToDateTime(yy,wk,...)` with Monday=1..Sunday=7 (§15.3.1.7) - and converts with `(d - Epoch).Days + 1` against Epoch 1601-01-01, which IS §15.5.2's integer date 1 (I confirmed 1601-01-01 is a Monday, and that 9999-12-31 is exactly 3,067,671 inclusive days later). THE NOTE IS HONOURED BY CONSTRUCTION: IntegerOfFormattedDate discards secondsScaled (`out _`), and the offset subfields feed no date adjustment, so a combined format's time portion is validated and cannot move the result - which is what Annex D.31.5.8 requires ("YYYYMMDD"/"19950215" and "YYYYMMDDThhmmss.ss+hhmm"/"19950215T05142781+0500" both -> 143951; I recomputed 143951 from the epoch). The result is typed integer: catalog IntrinsicType.Integer, IntrinsicRenderer#RenderNum returns NumX(..., scale 0).

TEST EVIDENCE - QUALIFYING, BUT THINNER THAN CLAIMED. Both refs are spec-derived and neither is a net: I read the helper at IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.cs:26 and AssertSpec compiles, runs and compares against a WRITTEN LITERAL - no legacy engine and no differential, despite the class name; the corpus golden's header states its own derivation. They cross-check rather than repeat, since 2021 day 167 IS 2021-06-16 and I recomputed 153569 from the §15.5.2 epoch independently. ⚠ BUT: BOTH write the §8.3.5 COMMA argument separator, never the space juxtaposition §15.48.2 prints; NOTHING exercises "YYYYMMDD", "YYYY-DDD", "YYYYWwwD" or "YYYY-Www-D" for this function; NOTHING exercises a COMBINED format for this function, so the §15.48.4 NOTE is verified by code reading ONLY and never by a test; and NEITHER §15.5.2 boundary is pinned - integer date 1 (1601-01-01) and 3,067,671 (9999-12-31, which is ISO 9999-W52-5, exactly ONE DAY short of the crash). Under the brief's rule 3 I did not reach for the GnuCOBOL differential (tests/external/gnucobol/tests/testsuite.src/run_functions.at:1725 does exercise this function) or any legacy comparison to close any of these.

EDITIONS derived from the STANDARD, not from IntrinsicCatalog's row: I grepped every occurrence of the name in specs/ISO_COBOL.md - the TOC, the §8.11 intrinsic-function-name list, Table 21 (:29941), §15.48, Annex D.31.5.8 and the index - and ANNEX E CARRIES NONE, so the function is not a 2023 addition and stands unchanged at 2014 and 2023. The 2002 boundary is not derivable from the 2023 text and is not asserted. ⚙ FIXED AND CLOSED 2026-08-05 (fix-queue PB23). This row's ONLY divergence was the shared week-date reconstruction, and the row itself said so ("ONE ROOT CAUSE, ONE FIX"). CobolDate#Analyze no longer calls ISOWeek.ToDateTime: §15.3.1.7 fixes week 1 as "the week that includes January 4", so that week's Monday is computed directly and every later day is a plain integer offset from it — the arithmetic CANNOT overflow, which is the point, because the input is VALID and no tightening of the per-subfield range table could have prevented the fault. The result is then range-checked against §15.5.2's ceiling ("shall be greater than zero and shall be less than or equal to ... 3,067,671"), and ONLY the caller that must PRODUCE an integer date form reacts: INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE raises EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION through ExceptionState#ArgumentError per §15.3 rule 14's "incorrect value ... FOR THE RETURNED VALUE" arm (implementor-defined result 0 when checking is off), while TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME still answers 0 — §15.92.4 requires any non-zero answer to be "the ordinal character position at which the first error ... was detected", and no CHARACTER of "9999W526" is in error (the identical '6' in "2009W526" is valid) — and SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME still returns its seconds (§15.79.4 reads only the time subfields). THE TWO-DAY WINDOW THIS ROW RECORDS (d=6 AND d=7) IS CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT, not re-derived on paper: 9999-12-31 is ISO 9999-W52-5. The new arithmetic is proven EQUIVALENT to ISOWeek over >200,000 week dates spanning 1601-9999 by unit:CobolDateIntegerDateRangeTests.TheIntegerWeekArithmetic_AgreesWithISOWeek_Everywhere, which asserts its own population so it cannot pass vacuously. ⛔ THE TEST GAP THIS ROW NAMED IS ALSO CLOSED: the golden carries Annex D.31.5.8's and D.31.5.9's OWN worked examples — "YYYYMMDD"/"19950215" and "YYYYMMDDThhmmss.ss+hhmm"/"19950215T05142781+0500" both -> 143951, and "hhmmss.ss+hhmm"/"05142781+0500" and its combined form both -> 18867.81 — so the §15.48.4 / §15.79.4 NOTE that the other half "does not impact the returned value" is now verified by TEST rather than by code reading.
